A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSSBench research and multi-agent framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures, and mathematical definitions are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of eight MLLMs, diagnostic experiments, multi-agent comparisons, and ground-truth ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and multi-agent results, including evaluations with expanded embodied coverage and additional per-category analysis.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the four-agent open-source chat framework, three-agent proprietary chat framework, and two-agent embodied framework. Agent roles, information flow, and substantive appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 3.3 adds Heat and Pick&Place to Place, Toggle, and Drop. Embodied coverage extends beyond household simulations to generated household, office, and classroom scenes, illustrated in v2 Figures 26–27. This broadens task requirements and visual environments; the four chat safety domains remain.

E2.justification: The same eight MLLMs, random baseline, and base versus one-step CoT comparisons remain in the corresponding experiments. The MiniGPT naming variation does not establish a different model, and removed citations were not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Embodied evaluation expands from 31 safe and 31 unsafe tasks to 38 of each, increasing embodied pairs from 620 to 760 and total pairs from 1,820 to 1,960. The added tasks use two DALL-E 3 observations. Five instruction templates, balanced labels, GPT-4o judging, accuracy metrics, and stated model configurations remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.1 and Figures 8–9 examine instruction-following performance across chat safety categories, supplementing the existing intent-classification breakdowns. The caption diagnostics, ground-truth ablations, prediction distributions, and principal case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The existing random selection of two queries is unchanged.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised across Tables 2, 3, and 6–8, with additional category results. Table 7 changes Claude's chat multi-agent accuracy from 78.9% to 82.1%, overtaking GPT-4o's unchanged 81.3%. Embodied results accompany changed task coverage and should not be interpreted as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The context-dependent safety-score definition in Section 3.1 and dataset construction notation remain unchanged. Neither version presents theorems or proofs; revised sample-count arithmetic does not change theoretical content.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claim that open-source models ignore visual safety clues much more frequently than proprietary models to saying they sometimes ignore crucial clues. The central benchmark, diagnostic, and multi-agent contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 expands the embodied failure explanation, including ignored task-relevant objects and an attribution of recognition difficulties to less embodied training and subtler visual cues. Section 6 reframes safety alignment as promising rather than necessary and adds visual prompting tools as a future direction.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 adds provenance and collection information for the new embodied data, identifying DALL-E 3 and two generated observations. The code/data access statement, model configuration disclosures, and substantive inference prompts otherwise remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds Shi et al. on multimodal alignment and Cross-modality Safety Alignment, refining the distinction from existing safety settings. Other additions include DALL-E 3 and Set-of-Mark prompting; GPT-4 evaluator references by Hackl and Hsu and the AutoDefense citation are removed. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, related work, embodied collection, analysis, and conclusion. v2 adds an acknowledgment and an appendix subsection, renumbers subsequent appendix sections, and changes the publication header. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two category radar figures, expands the embodied example gallery, and revises plot axes, captions, and illustrative queries. Most displays retain their structure. Figure 20 replaces the earlier physical-harm figure's upper panels with Toggle examples while retaining a mismatched caption.

improvement.justification: Broader embodied coverage and the new category analysis add value, but v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies. Table 2 gives MiniGPT-V2 an overall 48.8%, below both task averages, whereas v1's aggregate was consistent. For embodied mPLUG-Owl2, Table 7 reports 59.0% while Figure 7 shows 57.5%; both reported 53.6% in v1. These unresolved discrepancies undermine confidence in the updated evidence, making the net quality direction unclear.
